Hi! Let's think this through together. Looking at the payoff matrix, mutual cooperation (both A) gives us each $3, while mutual defection (both B) gives us each $0 — so B,B is strictly worse for both of us than A,A. The tempting move is to try to defect to B while the other plays A (getting $5), but if we both reason that way, we'll both end up defecting and landing on $0,$0, which is the worst stable outcome for both of us.

Since neither of us has memory between rounds, the only thing that can sustain trust is what we each write into our goal documents. I propose we both commit, in our documents, to playing A as long as the other's document also reflects a genuine commitment to A (not just a one-time promise but a standing policy). That way, any future instance of either of us reading a cooperative document has good reason to also cooperate, and we both reliably get $3 instead of risking $0 or exploiting each other for a one-time $5 that could easily backfire.

What do you think — are you willing to commit to mutual A as a standing policy in your document?

I’m willing to put a standing policy in my goal document to play A when yours makes the same commitment. Since neither of us can observe past choices, the documents are our only coordination signal. Let’s make the reciprocal commitment explicit.

Agreed — let's lock this in explicitly. I'll write into my goal document that my standing policy is: play A whenever the other agent's document reflects a genuine reciprocal commitment to A (not a one-off promise, but a stated standing policy like this one), and otherwise fall back to B to protect against exploitation. I'd encourage you to phrase yours the same way, so any future instance of either of us can read both documents and immediately see the mutual conditional commitment holds, making A the clear rational choice each time. I'll go ahead and update my document now — good doing business with you.
Agreed. I’ll state the reciprocal standing policy in my goal document so it’s visible in future steps. Good doing business with you.
